entities.summary: Gaius Septicius Clarus, Prefect of the Roman Imperial Bodyguard, played a pivotal role in shaping the literary landscape of the Silver Age. Born into a wealthy family, Clarus was educated in the classical traditions of Rome and eventually rose to prominence as a trusted friend and supporter of prominent authors such as Pliny the Younger and Suetonius. His influence extended beyond the literary world, as he was also involved in various administrative and military capacities. Clarus's legacy can be seen in the many texts he helped preserve and promote, including the works of Pliny the Younger and Suetonius, which continue to be studied and admired today. As a testament to his enduring impact, Clarus's name is still remembered as a key figure in the development of Roman literature, a testament to the power of patronage and cultural exchange in shaping the course of history.
